explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/769 ('Give good bounds for c(n)'): this variant asks whether log c(n)/(n log n) converges, on the n^n scale the problem sets. The known bounds 2^{n+1} - 1 ≤ c(n) ≪ n^{n+1} put the ratio in [0, 1] asymptotically. It is a reasonable, explicitly documented sharpening of the open 'good bounds' question, and excluding n = 0 is correctly justified. Faithful.
